provenance: Public creator/project pages reviewed October 23, 2026. Store ratings are native platform snapshots, not converted Steam percentages.

items.name: Quake Brutalist Jam III
items.summary: A colossal community FPS built around brutalist architecture, a replacement arsenal, expanded monsters, and 77 maps.
items.curatorWhy: One of the strongest free discoveries here: striking environments and a full-sized collection, not just a short demo.

items.requirements: Choose QBJ3 v1.3 STANDALONE for the bundled Windows game. That package uses LibreQuake assets and does not require an owned copy of Quake. The separate mod build has different requirements.
items.updateNote: Standalone v1.3 download added March 21, 2026. Original jam release: January 3, 2026.

items.name: Ashes 2063 / Afterglow
items.summary: Post-apocalyptic GZDoom campaigns mixing old-school gunplay with scavenging, ruined settlements, and wasteland exploration.
items.curatorWhy: Start here for the free underground scene: a substantial world and atmosphere rather than another arena-only shooter.
items.requirements: Use the official standalone compilation for the bundled game. Individual episode or add-on packages require the corresponding Ashes files and compatible GZDoom setup.
items.updateNote: The official standalone compilation includes the released episodes and expansions; Blackwater is a separate 2026 add-on.

items.name: Ashes: Blackwater
items.summary: An alternate-timeline Ashes add-on that reconnects six existing Afterglow and Hard Reset maps into a tougher hub-based adventure.
items.curatorWhy: A genuinely recent reason to revisit Ashes. Expect remixed spaces, new dialogue, and a demanding night in Atlanta, not six wholly new maps.
items.requirements: The June 20, 2026 v1.5 download is packaged as a standalone. Extract it and use its included launcher .bat. Hardcore mode requires the supplied GZDoom/config and its launcher. Earlier releases used a different setup.
items.updateNote: Version 1.5, updated June 20, 2026, adopts a standalone package. Six remixed Afterglow/Hard Reset maps form a hub, rather than six newly made maps.

items.name: Tremor: An Alternate Version of Quake
items.seedName: Tremor: An Alternate Version of Quake
items.summary: A four-episode, 32-map reimagining of Quake, revisiting familiar ideas through newly constructed environments.
items.curatorWhy: A big 2026 campaign for someone who wants more Quake exploration rather than a new storefront purchase.

items.name: Death Wish for Blood
items.summary: A substantial fan campaign for Blood with occult environments, secret hunting, and a major 2.0 overhaul in 2026.
items.curatorWhy: A must-investigate pick for Blood fans. The new overhaul matters more than its original 2011 launch date.

items.requirements: Requires Blood. The creator lists DOS, NBlood, Raze, BuildGDX, Fresh Supply, and Refreshed Supply support; use the matching instructions for your edition.
items.updateNote: Major 2.0 release: March 19, 2026. Version 2.0.1 update: June 22, 2026.

items.name: Dwell
items.summary: A sprawling Quake conversion with ancient architecture, a reworked arsenal, unusual monsters, and exploration-heavy campaigns.
items.curatorWhy: One of the richer Quake-world discoveries. The released episodes are substantial, but the planned four-episode project is not presented as complete.
items.requirements: Requires Quake and a compatible enhanced source port. Use the creator-recommended engine and installation instructions.
items.updateNote: Episode 2 was released February 4, 2023. Two released episodes are documented; the larger four-episode plan is still distinct.

items.name: Arcane Dimensions
items.summary: A Quake expansion framework and map collection focused on intricate levels, alternate routes, new enemies, and environmental storytelling.
items.curatorWhy: The essential older counterweight to the newest jams: worth keeping beside Dwell and QBJ3 for its imaginative level design.
items.requirements: Requires Quake game data and a source port supported by the chosen Arcane Dimensions release. Read that release's instructions.

items.name: Wolfenstein: Blade of Agony
items.summary: A free, story-driven WWII FPS campaign built with GZDoom, combining missions, secrets, and cinematic presentation.
items.curatorWhy: A substantial standalone campaign outside the big stores. Its ambitious presentation makes it more than a quick nostalgia experiment.
items.requirements: Choose the official standalone distribution for the bundled game. The separate mod package needs the documented GZDoom setup.

items.name: Project Osiris
items.summary: A free remake of Alien Breed 3D in GZDoom, rebuilding its 16-level campaign with modern controls and lighting.
items.curatorWhy: An excellent deep cut for chunky sci-fi environments and deliberate exploration, particularly if you missed the Amiga original.
items.requirements: The Windows download includes GZDoom and the game. No Doom II WAD is required. Other operating systems need a compatible GZDoom installation.
items.updateNote: Version 1.0.3 is documented in the May 11, 2021 development log.
warnings: Community rating has a small sample

items.name: Doom: The Golden Souls Remastered
items.summary: A colorful Doom II adventure that sends you through paintings into platforming-heavy worlds, now represented by its remastered edition.
items.curatorWhy: A creative change of pace when you want secrets, jumping challenges, and whimsical worlds instead of another grim industrial corridor.

items.name: Castlevania: Simon's Destiny
items.summary: A free first-person Castlevania reinterpretation built around whip combat, familiar monsters, and platforming.
items.curatorWhy: A stylish adjacent pick, not a conventional gun shooter. Its handcrafted first-person reinterpretation makes it a worthwhile hidden discovery.
items.requirements: Requires GZDoom, but the creator states no Doom game IWAD is needed.
items.updateNote: The creator download currently lists version 1.4.

items.name: Shrine
items.summary: A compact, surreal Doom-engine FPS through grotesque environments, strange creatures, and an unconventional arsenal.
items.curatorWhy: An approachable free introduction to Scumhead's horror work. The original Shrine belongs here even though its sequel has a Steam listing.
items.requirements: Use the creator's standalone Windows or Linux package. No paid Doom copy is listed as a prerequisite.

items.name: POOM
items.summary: A remarkably compact PICO-8 reinvention of Doom, playable in a browser or as a downloadable build.
items.curatorWhy: A genuinely unusual browser-first gem. It trades modern fidelity for clever design and an impressive sense of place within tiny technical limits.
items.requirements: Play in a compatible browser or use the creator's downloadable build. No separate Doom installation is required.

items.name: GUN GODZ
items.summary: A compact retro FPS built for fast runs, aggressive gunplay, and a distinctive Venusian-rap soundtrack.
items.curatorWhy: A sharp, free older pick from Vlambeer. Best approached as a replayable score-and-speed challenge rather than a long story campaign.
items.requirements: Download the standalone creator build for your operating system.

items.name: Siren
items.summary: A horror-oriented Doom II total conversion with a heavier emphasis on atmosphere and tense encounters.
items.curatorWhy: A promising mod-scene discovery for horror FPS fans; it is deliberately separated from the fastest movement shooters.
items.requirements: Requires Doom II game data and the GZDoom version specified by the creator. Check the creator page for the current package and setup.
items.updateNote: Public build 0.91b: February 12, 2026. The creator still labels the project in development.

items.name: Brutal Doom
items.summary: A combat overhaul for classic Doom with expanded weapon behavior, more forceful feedback, and much more graphic enemy reactions.
items.curatorWhy: Keep it as a gameplay-mod recommendation, not a separate campaign. Pair it only with maps and other mods whose compatibility is documented.
items.requirements: Requires compatible Doom game data and an engine supported by the selected release. Other gameplay mods can conflict.
items.updateNote: Stable v21 is separate from v22 Beta Test 6, published April 1, 2026. Choose a version deliberately and read its included manual.

items.name: VietDoom - Public Alpha
items.summary: A publicly available Vietnam-themed Doom conversion experimenting with larger combat spaces and tactical systems.
items.curatorWhy: An experimental deep cut, not a polished 2026 standalone release. The old public alpha and the creator's later standalone ambitions are different products.
items.requirements: The public legacy alpha is a Doom II mod. Follow its documented base-game and engine requirements.
items.updateNote: Public Alpha 3 is dated November 5, 2020. Later creator discussions about a standalone project do not make this alpha a full release.

items.name: Total Chaos - Original GZDoom Mod
items.summary: An atmospheric survival-horror conversion with scavenging, crafting, and dangerous encounters in an abandoned industrial setting.
items.curatorWhy: A striking example of what the Doom mod scene can build, but slower and more survival-focused than a typical boomer shooter.
items.requirements: Original free GZDoom Director's Cut 1.40, not the separate Unreal Engine remake. The official package includes GZDoom and does not require Total Chaos 1.0 or DOOM2.WAD.
items.updateNote: Original mod Director's Cut 1.40: August 8, 2022. The later commercial remake has a separate release history.

items.name: KAUNA - Creator Prototype
items.summary: A Finnish retro FPS about reclaiming your cottage and sauna from invading demons, available as a free work-in-progress build.
items.curatorWhy: A characterful tiny-audience discovery. Try the prototype first rather than treating a handful of ratings as proof of a finished hit.
items.requirements: Standalone downloadable prototype. The creator labels it a work in progress.
warnings: Community rating has a small sample

items.name: Wanted 3D: Dead or Alive - Demo
items.summary: A spaghetti-western retro FPS preview with bandits, secret hunting, period weapons, and a revenge-story setup.
items.curatorWhy: A fun-looking offbeat prospect for the demo shelf. The advertised full-game campaign features are not being passed off as the size of the demo.
